subject.title: fix(shared): skip app-group identity migration when OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR is overridden

question: Should OpenClaw treat an explicit `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` as an isolated caller-chosen store that never imports App Group identity/auth during fallback migration?
rationale: The change matches the existing legacy-fallback comment and fixes test/token leakage, but it changes behavior for any override-based run that previously inherited App Group identity/auth state.

options.title: Accept override isolation
options.body: Merge this direction so explicit state-dir overrides start from their chosen store and never silently import machine App Group pairing state.

options.title: Require more upgrade proof
options.body: Ask for focused before/after proof that override-based runs stay isolated while ordinary non-override legacy fallback still migrates identity and auth.

options.title: Pause for compatibility policy
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` to behave as a relocated install that may intentionally import existing App Group identity/auth.

recommendation.title: Accept override isolation
recommendation.body: Merge this direction so explicit state-dir overrides start from their chosen store and never silently import machine App Group pairing state.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored this follow-up and the prior auth-file migration fixup, and is assigned on the protected maintainer-labeled PR.
